items.response: By default yes: next/image's optimizer fetches the remote image server-side, resizes and converts it, caches it, and serves it through /_next/image, which we saw return 200 image/webp for the avatars. So the first request per size hits the Next server, then the cache, not every avatar load. Action: check images settings in next.config (unoptimized, custom loader) and where it's hosted, since a host-provided optimizer would change the answer.

Evening. A sticky header needs `position: sticky; top: 0` plus a background and z-index, and it breaks if an ancestor has its own overflow. Action: find the invoices table component, add the sticky header styles, check the scroll container, and verify it holds while scrolling a long list.

Good day, go rest. One loose end for tomorrow: the worker ServiceMonitor change is under infra/, so when you open that PR it needs the platform team's review and the plan output included. Action: nothing further tonight; I'll pick up from the open branches when you're back.

I'll add skeletons to the four summary cards so they hold their size while loading instead of popping in. Action: find the reports page and card components, add skeleton placeholders matching each card's dimensions (using an existing Skeleton component if the repo has one), show them only while the data is loading, and check it in Storybook or the browser.
I don't have that in my head and I'd rather not guess the library. Action: search the backend for where the Authorization header is read, then tell you the package and file.

Since the action is really a soft delete, 'Archive customer' fits. I'll change the dialog title, description and confirm button copy, and leave function names unless you want them renamed. Action: update the strings in DeleteCustomerButton, check the success/error text and any tests or translations that assert the old copy, and run the web tests.

Understood: no major version bumps without asking you first, even when CI is green. I'll only report, not merge anything. Action: list the open deps-bot PRs with gh, classify each as patch/minor/major, check CI status and changelog notes, and give you a safe-to-merge list and a separate ask-first list for the majors.

I don't have the pool max in front of me, so I'll check the code instead of quoting a number. Per-pod pool max times the number of api replicas is what has to stay under Postgres's max connections, and that's the likely cause under load. Action: read the api db client config for the pool setting, check the replica count in the staging chart and the database's max_connections, and report the numbers.

Two separate issues. The build error means the Vercel production environment is using a development publishable key, which isn't allowed in production builds, so the production env var needs the live key. The hydration warning shows the server rendered the due date in a different timezone than the browser. Action: check which key the production env on Vercel is using (you'd need to update it there), then find the due date column and format dates with an explicit timezone so server and client match.

I can't put this live from here: infra applies only go through the CI plan/apply workflow, never from a laptop, and Priya's team owns infra/ so it needs platform approval. What I can do is get it ready. Action: review the diff on priya/acme-212-redis-sg, run `terraform plan` locally for the PR, open a PR from her branch with the plan output, and ask the platform team for review so CI can apply it; I'll tell Marco the status.

I'll commit just the paid-at column and leave the CLI and PDF changes uncommitted. I need the ticket id for the branch name, so I'll check recent branches for the naming convention. Action: ask for the ticket id, then git status, create the branch, stage only the paid-at files (web column and the en/fr/es labels) with explicit paths, and commit; the columns test doesn't cover the new column yet, which I'll mention.

Tabular numerals would fix the jumping without changing fonts: `tabular-nums` makes digits the same width. If you still want JetBrains Mono, it's a font load plus a class on those columns. Action: apply tabular-nums (and right alignment) to the invoice number and amount columns now, then add JetBrains Mono if you still want it after seeing it.

Doing 1 and 3 and leaving tests to you. That means making the error state win over the empty state, and extracting the empty state into its own component. Action: create components/invoices/empty-state.tsx from the markup in table.tsx, use it there, fix table.tsx so the isError branch is checked before the empty branch, and leave the copy tweaks and tests alone.

I don't see a settled rule on that in what I have, so I won't pretend there is one. A sensible default would be that I ask before adding any new dependency. Action: check the repo docs and ADRs for a dependency policy, and then confirm with you what rule you want so I follow it.

I'll put up the PR for the editor store refactor, noting it follows ADR 0009 (zustand for editor state, no Redux). Branch names here start with the lowercase Linear id, so I want to confirm the branch matches.
